The simplest way to think about it: Qi2 is the magnetic wireless-charging standard, Qi2.2 is its faster 25W upgrade, and MagSafe is Apple's magnetic charging technology and accessory ecosystem. They overlap, so you don't necessarily have to choose just one.

Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe
1. Qi2
Up to 15W

The original magnetic version of the modern Qi wireless-charging standard, launched in 2023. Magnets align your phone with the charger for more reliable, efficient charging.

Works across supported phones and certified chargers.

A good choice for everyday charging.

Generally slower than Qi2.2 or newer 25W MagSafe chargers.

Source: Wireless Power Consortium

2. Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W)
Up to 25W

The faster generation of Qi2, introduced in 2025. Its official branding is Qi2 25W, based on the Qi 2.2.1 specification.

Nearly 70% more maximum power than 15W Qi2.

Certified chargers can charge compatible phones much faster.

Actual speed depends on your phone, charger and power adapter.

Source: Wireless Power Consortium

3. MagSafe
Up to 25W on supported models

Apple's magnetic charging technology, introduced with the iPhone 12. It includes magnetic alignment and a broader ecosystem of accessories, such as wallets, stands, batteries and chargers.

Designed to snap securely onto compatible iPhones.

Newer Apple MagSafe chargers are also certified for Qi2 25W.

Maximum charging speed depends on the iPhone and power adapter.

Source: Apple MagSafe Charger

What should you buy?

Best for Apple's ecosystem: Apple MagSafe Charger

$49 listed for the 2-meter version

A good option if you want Apple's own charger and support for up to 25W on compatible iPhones with a suitable adapter. The adapter is sold separately.

Best for charging three Apple devices: ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Qi2.2 25W

$99.99 listed; $82 with code PARTNER18

Charges a compatible phone, Apple Watch and earbuds in one stand. The included 50W adapter and active cooling are useful extras. The advertised 25W phone charging is limited to certain models.

Three things to check before buying

Your phone matters most. A 25W charger won't automatically deliver 25W to every phone.

Magnetic attachment isn't universal. Some Android phones need a compatible magnetic case, and Qi2 Ready phones may require one for full functionality.

Check the certification, not just the word “magnetic.” A Qi2 or Qi2.2-certified charger provides a clearer assurance of standards compliance and interoperability.

For the official standard details, see the Wireless Power Consortium's Qi overview.

My recommendation: If you have a compatible newer iPhone and want the fastest wireless charging, look for a certified Qi2 25W/Qi2.2 charger or a compatible 25W MagSafe charger. If you tell me your exact phone model, I can narrow down which one will actually charge it fastest.
